children.text: Tidal torques transfer Earth's spin angular momentum to the Moon's orbit. Treat the Moon as a point mass on a circular orbit about Earth's centre. The spin and orbital axes are parallel. Ignore the Sun and Earth's motion about the common centre of mass. All moments and torques refer to Earth's axis. Suffix 1 denotes present quantities and suffix 2 denotes the final synchronous state. Use \(M_E=6.0\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(M_M=7.3\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(D_1=3.8\times10^8\,\mathrm m\), \(\omega_{E1}=7.3\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), \(\omega_{M1}=2.7\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), and \(G=6.7\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{m^3kg^{-1}s^{-2}}\). Model Earth by density \(\rho_i=1.3\times10^4\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\) for \(r<r_i=3.5\times10^6\,\mathrm m\), and \(\rho_o=4.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\) up to \(r_o=6.4\times10^6\,\mathrm m\). Give numerical results to two significant figures.
Express \(L_2\), when both angular frequencies equal \(\omega_2\).
Write the conservation equation, neglecting the final Earth spin.
Find \(D_2\) using \(L_1,M_E,M_M,G\). Neglect final Earth spin throughout section 2.
Give \(D_2\) in metres and in units of \(D_1\).
Give \(\omega_2\) and the final day in present days.
Find final Earth spin divided by final Moon orbital angular momentum.

children.text: Model the tidal bulges as two point masses \(m=3.6\times10^{16}\,\mathrm{kg}\) on opposite points of Earth's surface. Their line leads the Earth-Moon line by \(\theta=3^\circ\). Find the force magnitude from the nearer bulge.
Find the force from the farther bulge.
Find the magnitude of the nearer-bulge torque.
Find the magnitude of the farther-bulge torque.
Find the leading nonzero net torque for \(r_o\ll D_1\). You may use \((1+u)^a\simeq1+au\).
Find the increase in separation per year, using \(1\,\mathrm{yr}=3.1\times10^7\,\mathrm s\).
Find the annual change in spin frequency and in the day length.
Find total rotational plus gravitational energy in terms of the present parameters.
Express \(\Delta E\) in terms of \(\Delta D_1,\Delta\omega_{E1}\), then evaluate it for one year.
Assume all Earth is covered by a layer of water of thickness \(h=0.5\,\mathrm m\), density \(10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\). Find its mass.

The layer rises by \(0.5\,\mathrm m\) twice daily, with 10 percent of gravitational energy dissipated when it falls. Use \(g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\) and 365 days per year. Find annual heat and compare with 4b.

statement.text:
Evolution of Earth-Moon system
Tidal torques transfer Earth's spin angular momentum to the Moon's orbit. Treat the Moon as a point mass on a circular orbit about Earth's centre. The spin and orbital axes are parallel. Ignore the Sun and Earth's motion about the common centre of mass. All moments and torques refer to Earth's axis. Suffix 1 denotes present quantities and suffix 2 denotes the final synchronous state. Use \(M_E=6.0\times10^{24}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(M_M=7.3\times10^{22}\,\mathrm{kg}\), \(D_1=3.8\times10^8\,\mathrm m\), \(\omega_{E1}=7.3\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), \(\omega_{M1}=2.7\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), and \(G=6.7\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{m^3kg^{-1}s^{-2}}\). Model Earth by density \(\rho_i=1.3\times10^4\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\) for \(r<r_i=3.5\times10^6\,\mathrm m\), and \(\rho_o=4.0\times10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\) up to \(r_o=6.4\times10^6\,\mathrm m\). Give numerical results to two significant figures.
1a. Present angular momentum
Express \(L_1\) using \(I_E,I_{M1},\omega_{E1},\omega_{M1}\).
1b. Synchronous angular momentum
Express \(L_2\), when both angular frequencies equal \(\omega_2\).
1c. Angular momentum conservation
Write the conservation equation, neglecting the final Earth spin.
2a. Final circular orbit
Write the gravitational circular-orbit equation.
2b. Final separation
Find \(D_2\) using \(L_1,M_E,M_M,G\). Neglect final Earth spin throughout section 2.
2c. Final angular frequency
Find \(\omega_2\) using the same parameters.
2d. Layered Earth inertia
Derive \(I_E\) for the two-density model.
2e. Earth inertia value
Evaluate the moment of inertia.
2f. Total angular momentum value
Evaluate the present angular momentum.
2g. Final separation value
Give \(D_2\) in metres and in units of \(D_1\).
2h. Final day
Give \(\omega_2\) and the final day in present days.
2i. Neglected spin ratio
Find final Earth spin divided by final Moon orbital angular momentum.
3a. Near-bulge force

Model the tidal bulges as two point masses \(m=3.6\times10^{16}\,\mathrm{kg}\) on opposite points of Earth's surface. Their line leads the Earth-Moon line by \(\theta=3^\circ\). Find the force magnitude from the nearer bulge.
3b. Far-bulge force
Find the force from the farther bulge.
3c. Near-bulge torque
Find the magnitude of the nearer-bulge torque.
3d. Far-bulge torque
Find the magnitude of the farther-bulge torque.
3e. Net tidal torque
Find the leading nonzero net torque for \(r_o\ll D_1\). You may use \((1+u)^a\simeq1+au\).
3f. Torque value
Evaluate the torque.
3g. Annual recession
Find the increase in separation per year, using \(1\,\mathrm{yr}=3.1\times10^7\,\mathrm s\).
3h. Spin slowdown and day length
Find the annual change in spin frequency and in the day length.
4a. System energy
Find total rotational plus gravitational energy in terms of the present parameters.
4b. Annual mechanical energy change
Express \(\Delta E\) in terms of \(\Delta D_1,\Delta\omega_{E1}\), then evaluate it for one year.
4c. Mass of tidal water
Assume all Earth is covered by a layer of water of thickness \(h=0.5\,\mathrm m\), density \(10^3\,\mathrm{kg/m^3}\). Find its mass.
4d. Annual tidal heat
The layer rises by \(0.5\,\mathrm m\) twice daily, with 10 percent of gravitational energy dissipated when it falls. Use \(g=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s^2}\) and 365 days per year. Find annual heat and compare with 4b.

children.text: Add a uniform outer-density sphere and an inner sphere of excess density: \[I_E=\frac{8\pi}{15}[\rho_or_o^5+(\rho_i-\rho_o)r_i^5].\]
The ratio is \(I_E/(M_MD_2^2)\simeq1/260\), validating the approximation.
The law of cosines gives \(s_-^2=D_1^2+r_o^2-2D_1r_o\cos\theta\), hence \(F_c=GmM_M/s_-^2\).
The lever arm supplies another factor \(D_1r_o\sin\theta/s_-\). Thus \(\tau_c=GmM_MD_1r_o\sin\theta/s_-^3\).
The leading terms cancel in \(\tau_c-\tau_f\). The next terms give \[\tau=6GmM_Mr_o^2\sin\theta\cos\theta/D_1^3.\]
Differentiate \(L_M=M_M\sqrt{GM_ED}\). Then \(\Delta D=2\tau\Delta t\sqrt{D_1/(GM_E)}/M_M=0.034\,\mathrm m\) per year.

Angular momentum conservation gives \(\Delta\omega_{E1}=-\tau\Delta t/I_E=-1.6\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\). Since \(P_E=2\pi/\omega_E\), \(\Delta P_E/P_E=-\Delta\omega_E/\omega_E\), giving \(\Delta P_E=1.9\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm s\) per year.
The circular orbit has energy \(-GM_EM_M/(2D_1)\). Thus \[E=\frac12I_E\omega_{E1}^2-\frac{GM_EM_M}{2D_1}.\]
The heat is \(Q=0.1M_{\rm water}g(0.5\,\mathrm m)\times2\times365=9.3\times10^{19}\,\mathrm J\). It is comparable to the mechanical energy loss.

solution.text:
Evolution of Earth-Moon system
1a. Present angular momentum
The two parallel contributions add: \(L_1=I_E\omega_{E1}+I_{M1}\omega_{M1}\).
1b. Synchronous angular momentum
\(L_2=(I_E+I_{M2})\omega_2\).
1c. Angular momentum conservation
\(I_E\omega_{E1}+I_{M1}\omega_{M1}=I_{M2}\omega_2=L_1\).
2a. Final circular orbit
\(\omega_2^2D_2^3=GM_E\).
2b. Final separation
Since \(L_1=M_M\sqrt{GM_ED_2}\), \[D_2=\frac{L_1^2}{GM_EM_M^2}.\]
2c. Final angular frequency
Combine \(\omega_2=\sqrt{GM_E/D_2^3}\) with part 2b: \(\omega_2=G^2M_E^2M_M^3/L_1^3\).
2d. Layered Earth inertia
Add a uniform outer-density sphere and an inner sphere of excess density: \[I_E=\frac{8\pi}{15}[\rho_or_o^5+(\rho_i-\rho_o)r_i^5].\]
2e. Earth inertia value
\(I_E=8.0\times10^{37}\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2}\).
2f. Total angular momentum value
Use \(I_{M1}=M_MD_1^2\). The result is \(L_1=3.4\times10^{34}\,\mathrm{kg\,m^2/s}\).
2g. Final separation value
\(D_2=5.4\times10^8\,\mathrm m=1.4D_1\).
2h. Final day
\(\omega_2=1.6\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), corresponding to about 46 present days.
2i. Neglected spin ratio
The ratio is \(I_E/(M_MD_2^2)\simeq1/260\), validating the approximation.
3a. Near-bulge force
The law of cosines gives \(s_-^2=D_1^2+r_o^2-2D_1r_o\cos\theta\), hence \(F_c=GmM_M/s_-^2\).
3b. Far-bulge force
\(s_+^2=D_1^2+r_o^2+2D_1r_o\cos\theta\), so \(F_f=GmM_M/s_+^2\).
3c. Near-bulge torque
The lever arm supplies another factor \(D_1r_o\sin\theta/s_-\). Thus \(\tau_c=GmM_MD_1r_o\sin\theta/s_-^3\).
3d. Far-bulge torque
\(\tau_f=GmM_MD_1r_o\sin\theta/s_+^3\), acting opposite to \(\tau_c\).
3e. Net tidal torque
The leading terms cancel in \(\tau_c-\tau_f\). The next terms give \[\tau=6GmM_Mr_o^2\sin\theta\cos\theta/D_1^3.\]
3f. Torque value
\(\tau=4.1\times10^{16}\,\mathrm{N\,m}\).
3g. Annual recession
Differentiate \(L_M=M_M\sqrt{GM_ED}\). Then \(\Delta D=2\tau\Delta t\sqrt{D_1/(GM_E)}/M_M=0.034\,\mathrm m\) per year.
3h. Spin slowdown and day length
Angular momentum conservation gives \(\Delta\omega_{E1}=-\tau\Delta t/I_E=-1.6\times10^{-14}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\). Since \(P_E=2\pi/\omega_E\), \(\Delta P_E/P_E=-\Delta\omega_E/\omega_E\), giving \(\Delta P_E=1.9\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm s\) per year.
4a. System energy
The circular orbit has energy \(-GM_EM_M/(2D_1)\). Thus \[E=\frac12I_E\omega_{E1}^2-\frac{GM_EM_M}{2D_1}.\]
4b. Annual mechanical energy change
\[\Delta E=I_E\omega_{E1}\Delta\omega_{E1}+\frac{GM_EM_M}{2D_1^2}\Delta D_1\simeq-9.0\times10^{19}\,\mathrm J.\]
4c. Mass of tidal water
\(M_{\rm water}=4\pi r_o^2h\rho_{\rm water}=2.6\times10^{17}\,\mathrm{kg}\).
4d. Annual tidal heat
The heat is \(Q=0.1M_{\rm water}g(0.5\,\mathrm m)\times2\times365=9.3\times10^{19}\,\mathrm J\). It is comparable to the mechanical energy loss.
